data.long_meaning: Meganathan is a combination of two Tamil words - 'Megam' which means great, and 'Anathan' which means God. So, Meganathan can be translated to 'Mighty God'. The name Meganathan carries the meaning “Mighty God” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Tamil, Sanskrit. Parents who choose Meganathan usually hope their child will grow to embody mighty god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Meganathan, a powerful Chola king of the 11th century, is known for his military exploits. He extended the Chola Empire's territories and ruled from the capital city of Thanjavur (Rajaraja Chola I). He is also known for his patronage of temples, especially the famous Brihadeeswarar Temple at Thanjavur.

Meganathan, another revered figure in Hindu mythology, is said to be an incarnation of the god Vishnu, specifically in the form of Mahavishnu. According to the Mahabharata, he was born to help the Pandava prince Bhima, and aided him in his battles against the Kauravas.
